Among this is His oath by *al-'asr* (time) concerning the state of man in the Hereafter. This surah, despite its extreme brevity, is of great importance, so much so that al-Shafi'i (may God have mercy on him) said: "If people all reflected upon it, it would suffice them."

As for *al-'asr* by which He swears, it is said to be the first part of the time that follows the maghrib (sunset), from the day; and it is said to be the last hour of its hours; and it is said that what is meant is the 'asr prayer. But most of the mufassirun (exegetes) hold that it is time (al-dahr), and this is the preferred view. Calling time *'asr* is well known in their language. The poet said:

؎ولن يلبث العصران يوم وليلة ∗∗∗ إذا طلبا أن يدركا ما تيمما

(Neither of the two *'asr*s will tarry, a day and a night, when they seek to reach what they have set out for.)

"A day and a night" is an appositive substitute for "the two *'asr*s". So He, glorified is He, swore by time because of the lesson and the sign in it. For the passing of night and day, by the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing, orders the interests of the world in the most perfect arrangement and system; their alternation, now their equalization, now the taking of one from the other, their difference in light and darkness, heat and cold, the spreading of living creatures and their rest, and the division of time into centuries, years, months, days, hours and what is smaller, are a sign among the signs of the Lord, the Exalted, and a proof among the proofs of His power and wisdom.

So He swore by time, which is the period and the place of man's deeds, upon the outcome of those deeds and their recompense. And through the beginning, namely the creation of time, of the doers and of their deeds, He alerted to the Return, and that His power, just as it fell not short of the beginning, falls not short of the Return; and that His wisdom, which required the creation of time, of the doers and of their deeds, and made them two kinds, good and evil, refuses that they be treated alike, and refuses that the doer of good not be recompensed for his good,

nor the doer of evil for his evil, or that both kinds be made winners or both losers. Rather man, insofar as he is man, is a loser, except those whom God has had mercy upon, guiding them and granting them success in faith and righteous action in themselves, and in enjoining others to it. This is parallel to His returning man to the lowest of the low, and excepting from those so returned those who believed and did righteous deeds.

Consider the wisdom of the Qur'an: when He said ﴿Indeed, man is in loss﴾, He narrowed the exception and specified it, saying ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds and enjoin one another to the truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾. But when He said ﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾, He widened the exception and made it general, saying ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, and did not say "and enjoin one another". For mutual enjoining is commanding others to faith and righteous action, which is an addition beyond merely doing it oneself. Whoever is not so has lost this gain, so he is in loss, though it does not follow that he is in the lowest of the low. For a person may fulfil what is obligatory upon him and not command others; commanding the good and forbidding the evil is an added rank, and it may be an individual obligation, a communal obligation, or recommended.

Mutual enjoining of the truth includes the truth that is obligatory and the truth that is recommended, and patience includes the patience that is obligatory and that which is recommended. So when these enjoin the truth and enjoin patience, they attain a gain that was lost by those who fulfilled what was obligatory upon them in themselves but did not command others to it, even though those were not among the ones who have lost themselves and their families. Absolute loss is one thing, and loss in the unqualified sense is another. He, glorified is He, only said ﴿Indeed, man is in loss﴾. One who profits in one commodity and loses in another may be described as being in loss and as having loss, as 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar (may God be pleased with them both) said: "We have fallen short regarding many qirats." This is a kind of shortcoming and a kind of loss relative to one who gained that profit.

When He said in Surat al-Tin ﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾, He said ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, dividing people into these two categories only. Since man has two faculties, the faculty of knowledge and the faculty of action, and two states, a state in which he takes commands from another and a state in which he commands another, He, glorified is He, excepted from man, who is in loss, the one who perfected his faculty of knowledge by faith and his faculty of action by righteous deeds, who submitted to another's command to him to do so, and who commanded another to it. For the servant has two states: a state of perfection in himself and a state of perfecting another, and his perfection and his perfecting of others depend on two things:

knowledge of the truth, and patience upon it. So the verse comprised all ranks of human perfection: beneficial knowledge, righteous action, doing good to oneself through them and to one's brother through them, and his submission to and acceptance from the one who commands him to that.

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿and enjoin one another to the truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾ is a guidance to the station of leadership (imama) in the strength of religion, like His saying, the Exalted, ﴿And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and were certain of Our signs﴾. By patience and certainty, leadership in religion is attained.

Patience is of two kinds: patience in what is decreed, such as calamities, and patience in what is legislated.

This latter is also of two kinds: patience in performing commands, and patience in refraining from prohibitions.

The former is patience upon willing and doing, and the latter is patience away from willing and doing.

As for the first kind of patience, it is shared between the believer and the disbeliever, the pious and the wicked; it is not rewarded in itself unless faith and choice accompany it.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning his daughter:

"Command her to be patient and to seek reward from God."

And the Exalted said ﴿except those who are patient and do righteous deeds; those will have forgiveness and a great reward﴾.

And the Exalted said ﴿Yes, if you are patient and fear God﴾.

And He said ﴿And if you are patient and fear God﴾.

So patience without faith and piety is like the strength of a body devoid of faith and piety, and in proportion to certainty in what is legislated is patience in what is decreed.

And the Exalted said ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of God is true, and let not those who have no certainty make you impatient﴾.

So He commanded him to be patient and not to resemble those who have no certainty in their lack of patience. For due to their lack of certainty they lack patience, and they became light and made their people light. Had certainty and the truth been attained by them, they would have been patient and would not have been light nor made others light. Whoever's certainty is little, his patience is little, and whoever's patience is little becomes light and makes others light. The certain and patient one is steady, because he possesses intellect and reason; while the one who has no certainty and no patience is light and rash, played with by whims and desires as winds play with a light object. And God is the one whose help is sought.

So the surah comprised the two counsels, the two perfectings, and the utmost perfection of the two faculties, in the most concise, brief and refined wording, the most beautiful in style and the most gracious in effect.

As for the two perfectings: his perfecting himself and his perfecting his brother.

and none of that is complete for it except through patience.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿By time, indeed man is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds and enjoin one another to the truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾

The explanation of that is that the ranks are four, and by completing them a person attains the utmost of his perfection:

The first is knowledge of the truth.

The second is acting upon it.

The third is teaching it to one who does not know it well.

The fourth is patience upon learning it, acting upon it and teaching it.

So the Exalted mentioned the four ranks in this surah. He, glorified is He, swore in this surah by time that everyone is in loss, except those who believed and did righteous deeds, and they are those who knew the truth and affirmed it; this is one rank.

(and did righteous deeds), and they are those who acted upon what they knew of the truth; this is another rank.

(and enjoined one another to the truth): they counseled one another with it by teaching and guidance; this is a third rank.

(and enjoined one another to patience): they were patient upon the truth, and counseled one another to patience upon it and steadfastness; this is a fourth rank.

And this is the utmost perfection, for perfection is that a person be perfect in himself and perfecting of others. His perfection is by setting right his two faculties, of knowledge and of action: the soundness of the knowledge faculty is by faith, and the soundness of the practical faculty is by doing righteous deeds; and his perfecting of others is by teaching it to them, his patience with them, and his counseling them to patience in knowledge and action.

He, glorified and exalted, swore by time, which is the period of profitable and losing deeds, that everyone is in loss, except one who perfected his knowledge faculty by faith in God, and his practical faculty by acting in obedience to Him. This is his perfection in himself. Then he perfected others by counseling them to that, commanding them to it, and to its mainstay, which is patience. So he perfected himself by beneficial knowledge and righteous action, and perfected others by teaching them that and counseling them to patience upon it.

He said in *al-Madarij*:

He, glorified is He, swore that everyone is a loser except one who perfected his knowledge faculty by faith, his practical faculty by righteous action, and perfected others by counseling them to the truth and to patience upon it. The truth is faith and action, and they are not complete except through patience upon them and mutual counsel to them. He, glorified is He, judged loss as a general judgment upon everyone who did not believe and was not among the people of truth and patience.

And this indicates that there is no winner besides them. So the Exalted said ﴿By time, indeed man is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds and enjoin one another to the truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾.

For this reason al-Shafi'i said: "If people all reflected upon this verse, it would encompass them."

And the anchor of that, its foundation and the stalk upon which it stands, is patience.

truth and patience, and they are the two mentioned in His saying, the Exalted ﴿and enjoin one another to the truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾.

(Section)

Gathering with brothers is of two kinds:

One: gathering for the sake of temperamental companionship and passing the time. The harm of this outweighs its benefit, and the least in it is that it corrupts the heart and wastes time.

Two: gathering with them for cooperating upon the means of salvation and enjoining one another to the truth and patience.

This is among the greatest and most beneficial gains, but it has three afflictions:

One: that they adorn themselves for one another.

Two: speech and mingling beyond what is needed.

Three: that it becomes a desire and habit by which one is cut off from the objective.

In sum, gathering and mingling is a fertilization, either of the soul that commands to evil (al-nafs al-ammara), or of the heart and the tranquil soul (al-nafs al-mutma'inna), and the result is derived from the fertilization; whoever seeks good fertilization, his fruit is good.

Likewise good spirits are fertilized by the angel, and evil ones are fertilized by Satan. And God, glorified is He, by His wisdom made good things for the good and the good for good things.

(Neither of the two *'asr*s will tarry, a day and a night, when they seek to reach what they have set out for.)

"A day and a night" is an appositive substitute for "the two *'asr*s". So He, glorified is He, swore by time because of the lesson and the sign in it. For the passing of night and day, by the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing, orders the interests of the world in the most perfect arrangement and system; their alternation, now their equalization, now the taking of one from the other, their difference in light and darkness, heat and cold, the spreading of living creatures and their rest, and the division of time into centuries, years, months, days, hours and what is smaller, are a sign among the signs of the Lord, the Exalted, and a proof among the proofs of His power and wisdom.

So He swore by time, which is the period and the place of man's deeds, upon the outcome of those deeds and their recompense. And through the beginning, namely the creation of time, of the doers and of their deeds, He alerted to the Return, and that His power, just as it fell not short of the beginning, falls not short of the Return; and that His wisdom, which required the creation of time, of the doers and of their deeds, and made them two kinds, good and evil, refuses that they be treated alike, and refuses that the doer of good not be recompensed for his good,

nor the doer of evil for his evil, or that both kinds be made winners or both losers. Rather man, insofar as he is man, is a loser, except those whom God has had mercy upon, guiding them and granting them success in faith and righteous action in themselves, and in enjoining others to it. This is parallel to His returning man to the lowest of the low, and excepting from those so returned those who believed and did righteous deeds.

Consider the wisdom of the Qur'an: when He said ﴿Indeed, man is in loss﴾, He narrowed the exception and specified it, saying ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds and enjoin one another to the truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾. But when He said ﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾, He widened the exception and made it general, saying ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, and did not say "and enjoin one another". For mutual enjoining is commanding others to faith and righteous action, which is an addition beyond merely doing it oneself. Whoever is not so has lost this gain, so he is in loss, though it does not follow that he is in the lowest of the low. For a person may fulfil what is obligatory upon him and not command others; commanding the good and forbidding the evil is an added rank, and it may be an individual obligation, a communal obligation, or recommended.

Mutual enjoining of the truth includes the truth that is obligatory and the truth that is recommended, and patience includes the patience that is obligatory and that which is recommended. So when these enjoin the truth and enjoin patience, they attain a gain that was lost by those who fulfilled what was obligatory upon them in themselves but did not command others to it, even though those were not among the ones who have lost themselves and their families. Absolute loss is one thing, and loss in the unqualified sense is another. He, glorified is He, only said ﴿Indeed, man is in loss﴾. One who profits in one commodity and loses in another may be described as being in loss and as having loss, as 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar (may God be pleased with them both) said: "We have fallen short regarding many qirats." This is a kind of shortcoming and a kind of loss relative to one who gained that profit.

When He said in Surat al-Tin ﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾, He said ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, dividing people into these two categories only. Since man has two faculties, the faculty of knowledge and the faculty of action, and two states, a state in which he takes commands from another and a state in which he commands another, He, glorified is He, excepted from man, who is in loss, the one who perfected his faculty of knowledge by faith and his faculty of action by righteous deeds, who submitted to another's command to him to do so, and who commanded another to it. For the servant has two states: a state of perfection in himself and a state of perfecting another, and his perfection and his perfecting of others depend on two things:

knowledge of the truth, and patience upon it. So the verse comprised all ranks of human perfection: beneficial knowledge, righteous action, doing good to oneself through them and to one's brother through them, and his submission to and acceptance from the one who commands him to that.

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿and enjoin one another to the truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾ is a guidance to the station of leadership (imama) in the strength of religion, like His saying, the Exalted, ﴿And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and were certain of Our signs﴾. By patience and certainty, leadership in religion is attained.

Patience is of two kinds: patience in what is decreed, such as calamities, and patience in what is legislated.

This latter is also of two kinds: patience in performing commands, and patience in refraining from prohibitions.

The former is patience upon willing and doing, and the latter is patience away from willing and doing.

As for the first kind of patience, it is shared between the believer and the disbeliever, the pious and the wicked; it is not rewarded in itself unless faith and choice accompany it.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning his daughter:

"Command her to be patient and to seek reward from God."

And the Exalted said ﴿except those who are patient and do righteous deeds; those will have forgiveness and a great reward﴾.

And the Exalted said ﴿Yes, if you are patient and fear God﴾.

And He said ﴿And if you are patient and fear God﴾.

So patience without faith and piety is like the strength of a body devoid of faith and piety, and in proportion to certainty in what is legislated is patience in what is decreed.

And the Exalted said ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of God is true, and let not those who have no certainty make you impatient﴾.

So He commanded him to be patient and not to resemble those who have no certainty in their lack of patience. For due to their lack of certainty they lack patience, and they became light and made their people light. Had certainty and the truth been attained by them, they would have been patient and would not have been light nor made others light. Whoever's certainty is little, his patience is little, and whoever's patience is little becomes light and makes others light. The certain and patient one is steady, because he possesses intellect and reason; while the one who has no certainty and no patience is light and rash, played with by whims and desires as winds play with a light object. And God is the one whose help is sought.

(Section)

He heard a reciter recite: ﴿By time (1) Indeed, man is in loss (2) except those who believe and do righteous deeds and enjoin one another to the truth and enjoin one another to patience (3)﴾

So he said: If people all took to this surah, it would encompass them or suffice them, as al-Shafi'i (may God be pleased with him) said: "If people reflected upon Surat al-'Asr, it would suffice them."

For He, glorified is He, divided mankind in it into two categories: loser and winner. The winner is the one who gave sincere counsel to himself through faith and righteous action, and gave sincere counsel to creation by enjoining the truth, which includes teaching and guiding them, and by enjoining patience, which includes his own patience as well. So the surah comprised the two counsels, the two perfectings, and the utmost perfection of the two faculties, in the most concise, brief and refined wording, the most beautiful in style and the most gracious in effect.

As for the two counsels: the servant's counsel to himself, and his counsel to his brother by enjoining the truth and patience upon it.

As for the two perfectings: his perfecting himself and his perfecting his brother.

As for the perfection of the two faculties: the soul has two faculties, the faculty of knowledge and reflection, whose perfection is by faith, and the faculty of will, love and action, whose perfection is by righteous action,

and none of that is complete for it except through patience.

So here there are six matters: three that he does in himself and commands others to: perfecting his knowledge faculty by faith, his practical faculty by righteous deeds, and persistence in that through patience; and his commanding others to these three. So he is one who is commanded by them, who commands them, who is characterized by them, who teaches them and calls to them. This is the one who gains the full gain, and whatever of the gain escapes him is according to that, and a kind of loss has befallen him. And God is the one whose help is sought and upon Him is reliance.

He said in *Miftah Dar al-Sa'ada*:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿By time, indeed man is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds and enjoin one another to the truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾

Al-Shafi'i (may God be pleased with him) said: "If people all reflected upon this surah, it would suffice them."

The explanation of that is that the ranks are four, and by completing them a person attains the utmost of his perfection:

The first is knowledge of the truth.

The second is acting upon it.

The third is teaching it to one who does not know it well.

The fourth is patience upon learning it, acting upon it and teaching it.

So the Exalted mentioned the four ranks in this surah. He, glorified is He, swore in this surah by time that everyone is in loss, except those who believed and did righteous deeds, and they are those who knew the truth and affirmed it; this is one rank.

(and did righteous deeds), and they are those who acted upon what they knew of the truth; this is another rank.

(and enjoined one another to the truth): they counseled one another with it by teaching and guidance; this is a third rank.

(and enjoined one another to patience): they were patient upon the truth, and counseled one another to patience upon it and steadfastness; this is a fourth rank.

And this is the utmost perfection, for perfection is that a person be perfect in himself and perfecting of others. His perfection is by setting right his two faculties, of knowledge and of action: the soundness of the knowledge faculty is by faith, and the soundness of the practical faculty is by doing righteous deeds; and his perfecting of others is by teaching it to them, his patience with them, and his counseling them to patience in knowledge and action.

So this surah, despite its brevity, is among the most comprehensive surahs of the Qur'an of all good in its entirety. Praise be to God who made His Book sufficient in place of everything else, a cure for every ailment, a guide to every good.

He said in *Ighathat al-Lahfan*:

He, glorified and exalted, swore by time, which is the period of profitable and losing deeds, that everyone is in loss, except one who perfected his knowledge faculty by faith in God, and his practical faculty by acting in obedience to Him. This is his perfection in himself. Then he perfected others by counseling them to that, commanding them to it, and to its mainstay, which is patience. So he perfected himself by beneficial knowledge and righteous action, and perfected others by teaching them that and counseling them to patience upon it.

He said in *al-Madarij*:

He, glorified is He, swore that everyone is a loser except one who perfected his knowledge faculty by faith, his practical faculty by righteous action, and perfected others by counseling them to the truth and to patience upon it. The truth is faith and action, and they are not complete except through patience upon them and mutual counsel to them. It is fitting for man to spend the hours of his life, indeed his very breaths, in what attains for him the lofty aims and delivers him from manifest loss. That is only by turning to the Qur'an, understanding it, reflecting upon it, extracting its treasures, unearthing its buried riches, devoting care to it, and devoting resolve to it. For it is the guarantor of the interests of servants in livelihood and the Return, and the one that conveys them to the path of right guidance. The reality (haqiqa) and the way (tariqa), the tastes (adhwaq) and the sound spiritual states (mawajid), none of them is taken except from its niche, nor harvested except from its trees.

He said in *'Uddat al-Sabirin*:

He, glorified is He, judged loss as a general judgment upon everyone who did not believe and was not among the people of truth and patience.

And this indicates that there is no winner besides them. So the Exalted said ﴿By time, indeed man is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds and enjoin one another to the truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾.

For this reason al-Shafi'i said: "If people all reflected upon this verse, it would encompass them."

That is because the servant's perfection lies in perfecting his two faculties, the faculty of knowledge and the faculty of action, and they are faith and righteous action.

And just as he needs to perfect himself, he needs to perfect others, and that is mutual enjoining of the truth and mutual enjoining of patience.

And the anchor of that, its foundation and the stalk upon which it stands, is patience.

(Benefit)

Know that religion is built upon two foundations:

truth and patience, and they are the two mentioned in His saying, the Exalted ﴿and enjoin one another to the truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾.

Since what is required of the servant is to act upon the truth in himself and to carry it out among people, and this is the reality of gratitude (shukr), he cannot do that except through patience upon it. So patience is half of faith. And God, glorified and exalted, knows best.

(Section)

Gathering with brothers is of two kinds:

One: gathering for the sake of temperamental companionship and passing the time. The harm of this outweighs its benefit, and the least in it is that it corrupts the heart and wastes time.

Two: gathering with them for cooperating upon the means of salvation and enjoining one another to the truth and patience.

This is among the greatest and most beneficial gains, but it has three afflictions:

One: that they adorn themselves for one another.

Two: speech and mingling beyond what is needed.

Three: that it becomes a desire and habit by which one is cut off from the objective.

In sum, gathering and mingling is a fertilization, either of the soul that commands to evil (al-nafs al-ammara), or of the heart and the tranquil soul (al-nafs al-mutma'inna), and the result is derived from the fertilization; whoever seeks good fertilization, his fruit is good.

Likewise good spirits are fertilized by the angel, and evil ones are fertilized by Satan. And God, glorified is He, by His wisdom made good things for the good and the good for good things.
